g.text: LHCb PicoCal Conical Light-Guide Inner-Surface Reconstruction & Optical Simulation
Bicubic B-Spline Freeform Surface + Apple Metal GPU Ray Tracing + Geant4 11.1.3 Validation (Wheel Zoom & Drag Pan)
Author: Hengne Li | Hengne.Li@cern.ch | Hengne.Li@m.scnu.edu.cn · SCNU / CERN LHCb
1. Optical Physics Diagnosis & Inverse Reconstruction Pipeline
• STEP Cone: Ø17.5 → Ø8.0 mm, L=100 mm
• Reflective Film ~311 μm, Beam σ=0.22 mm
• Exact C² Analytic Normal n(θ, z)
Key Physical Mechanism: Why Micron-Scale Inner Bulges Induce Strong 2D Scan Ripples
1. Etendue Limit: (4.0 / 8.75)² ≈ 20.9%; >99% of guided diffuse photons undergo 1–14 specular wall bounces;
2. Critical-Angle Lever: ~78% of rays turn around; a 150–200 μm bulge steepens upstream slope & triggers escape;
3. Axial Projection: Front bulges modulate outer rings; mid-rear bulges (z ∈ [40, 85] mm) shape central pits & crescents.
Quantitative Match: Shot-noise floor 0.81%, non-axisymmetric texture r = 0.8797, peak bulge -268 μm / dent +272 μm.
3. Entrance 100×100 Diffuse Laser Scan Comparison (Net Signal mV)
Dashed Circle: Effective Aperture R_eff = 8.439 mm | Upper-left dark pit & right bright crescent reproduced pixel-by-pixel
